content:
incident-bot: [ALERT] INC-1778882222 — p99 latency breach detected for streaming endpoints across us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Start=2024-10-12T03:14:22Z. Services: streaming.generate, streaming.kv-prefetch. p99 current=2400ms (SLO=800ms), p95 current=1200ms. Error spike: streaming stalls / tail latency.

maria-g: yep seeing the same in Dashboards -> per-route. Tail is dominated by long responses and a big increase in cache_miss counts.:eyes:

chris-b: FYI we had the prefix-hash v2 rollout in eu-west-1 around 02:45Z (gradual). Could be invalidation pattern + namespace salt change.

maria-g: logs show huge prefix churn + rekeys. sample log:
```
2024-10-12T03:10:34Z worker=stream-17 cache_miss=9243 prefix=ab3f12 path=/v1/streaming/generate latency_ms=2012
2024-10-12T03:11:02Z worker=stream-17 cache_invalidate prefix=ab3f12 reason=hash-update
```

kyle: I can flip prefetch off for live route to reduce write pressure on prefixcache. That should reduce backend saturation while we triage.

kevin: +1. Prefetch off + route-split to fallback cluster (no v2 prefix) for 10% traffic as canary. If latency improves we can escalate rollback.

infra-bot: deploy-checks: new-rollout:v2-prefix -> OK -> traffic-split=enabled.

maria-g: experimental quick check: increase cache TTL from 30s->5m for the streaming prefix cache in us-west-2 to see if hit rate improves. Will monitor hit-rate delta.

chris-b: I'm running kv hash inspector to see if salt mismatch caused namespace blowup. Commands: 
```bash
# check active salt versions by region
redwood infra kv-salt list --region us-west-2
redwood infra prefix-metrics inspect --prefix-sample ab3f12 --since 15m
```

maria-g: dashboards: cache_hit_rate (streaming) dropped from 92% -> 18% in the last 20 mins in eu-west-1. Also p99 latency correlated with cache_miss spikes.

support-bot: Customer impact: Support queue shows 6 customers reporting degraded streaming responses (long hangs / partial outputs). No customer-facing downtime but higher latency and partial streams. Raising CS escalation flag.

kyle: mitigation plan enacted: 1) flipped prefetch off on streaming.generate route in eu-west-1 at 03:22Z. 2) initiated a 10% traffic split to fallback cluster (no prefix-hash v2) at 03:25Z. 3) increased prefix cache TTL in us-west-2 at 03:28Z.

maria-g: immediate telemetry after actions: p95 down from 1200ms -> 750ms in fallback split, overall p99 decreased from 2400ms -> 1400ms but still above SLO. Cache hit rate in fallback cluster is stable ~89%.

chris-b: kv inspector output (snippet):
```
region: eu-west-1
active_salts: [v1, v2]
timestamp: 2024-10-12T03:12:00Z
hot_prefixes: 87
prefix_entropy: high
cache_namespace_count: +12%
```
Interpretation: v2 introduced namespace granularity change causing blowout in cold caches.

kevin: we need to decide: 1) rollback prefix-hash v2 rollout in eu-west-1 OR 2) pause rollout and backfill cache with warm-up. Rollback gives faster recovery for tail latency but loses the benefits of v2.

maria-g: agree. Rollback asap. I can trigger rollback of the prefix-hash rollout to previous stable config at 03:42Z if we greenlight.

kyle: go ahead with rollback. Meanwhile leave prefetch off and traffic split until we confirm p99 back under SLO.

infra-bot: rollback initiated: rollout:v2-prefix -> target eu-west-1 -> rollback to stable at 03:45Z. Status: in-progress.

incident-bot: Update: rollback progress: 60% -> 100% (completed 03:50Z).

maria-g: after rollback: p99 in eu-west-1 dropped to 820ms within 6 minutes. overall p99 across regions now 780ms. p95 stable ~600ms. Streaming stalls largely resolved.

support-bot: Customer impact update: tickets still open but no new reports in last 12 minutes. CS prioritization lowered to medium.

chris-b: root cause hypothesis: v2 prefix hashing increased namespace cardinality; coupled with simultaneous prefetch behavior and a burst of distinct long-tail keys, we flooded cold caches causing massive backend work and stalls on streaming handlers.

maria-g: next steps (short):
- Recreate exact workload in staging and run v2 prefix change with workload replay.
- Add safety guard: automatic slow-start when changing prefix hash that limits initial namespace growth (e.g., staged salt exposure).
- Improve prefetch backoff heuristics during prefix changes.

kyle: I'm taking ownership of the on-call handoff. Current state summary for next on-call (SRE night):
- Incident ID: INC-1778882222
- Start: 2024-10-12T03:14:22Z
- Action taken: prefetch off, traffic split to fallback, increased TTL, rollback of prefix-hash v2 in eu-west-1 (completed).
- Current status: stable, p99 ~780ms, monitoring for 30m.
- Owner: kyle (oncall) -> handoff to sre_jen at 04:00Z.
- TODOs: reproduce in staging, add safety guard, run cache warm-up script if re-rollout planned.

sre_jen: Acknowledge and taking handoff at 04:00Z. I'll watch for any regression during the next hour. I'll also schedule a post-incident review with eng-ml and infra next day.

maria-g: saving all graphs and snippets to incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian/incidents/INC-1778882222

kevin: ETA for full RCA doc and action items by EOD tomorrow.

sre_jen: Thanks everyone. Closing the on-call bridge for now but leaving monitoring alerts at paged-level until the morning. I'll post a short postmortem draft once we have the staging reproducer. :white_check_mark:
